logic_node.action_detail: Patients with clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis (LV wall thickness >=14 mm with fatigue, dyspnea, or edema) should have screening for serum and urine monoclonal light chains with serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE) and serum free light chains (FLC). Together, serum IFE, urine IFE, and serum FLC is >99% sensitive for AL amyloidosis.

source_text: Patients for whom there is a clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis should have screening for serum and urine monoclonal light chains with serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis and serum free light chains.

logic_node.action: Perform bone scintigraphy for ATTR-CM diagnosis
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with high clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis without evidence of serum or urine monoclonal light chains, bone scintigraphy (99mTc-PYP scan) should be performed to confirm the presence of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Grade 2/3 cardiac uptake or H/CL ratio >1.5 in the absence of monoclonal protein is diagnostic of ATTR-CM. SPECT should be assessed in all positive scans.

source_text: In patients with high clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis, without evidence of serum or urine monoclonal light chains, bone scintigraphy should be performed to confirm the presence of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with a diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), genetic testing with TTR gene sequencing is recommended to differentiate hereditary variant (ATTRv) from wild-type (ATTRwt) transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Differentiating ATTRv from ATTRwt is important for genetic counseling, family screening, and eligibility for therapies such as inotersen and patisiran (approved only for ATTRv with polyneuropathy).

source_text: In patients for whom a diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis is made, genetic testing with TTR gene sequencing is recommended to differentiate hereditary variant from wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.

logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with wild-type or variant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) and NYHA class I to III HF symptoms, tafamidis (transthyretin tetramer stabilizer) is indicated to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Available as tafamidis meglumine 80 mg (4x20 mg capsules) once daily or tafamidis 61 mg capsule once daily. Benefit not observed in NYHA class IV, severe aortic stenosis, or eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2. Greater benefit expected when administered early in disease course; survival curves separate after 18 months.

source_text: In select patients with wild-type or variant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and NYHA class I to III HF symptoms, transthyretin tetramer stabilizer therapy (tafamidis) is indicated to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

logic_node.action_detail: Tafamidis meglumine is available in 20 mg capsules; FDA-approved dose is 80 mg (4 capsules) once daily. Alternatively, tafamidis is available in 61 mg capsules with FDA-approved dose of 61 mg once daily.

source_text: Tafamidis meglumine is available in 20-mg capsules; and the FDA-approved dose is 80 mg (4 capsules) once daily. Tafamidis is also available in 61-mg capsules; the FDA-approved dose for this new formulation is 61 mg once daily.

logic_node.action: Avoid tafamidis in NYHA class IV
logic_node.action_detail: Benefit of tafamidis has not been observed in patients with NYHA class IV symptoms. Tafamidis should be reserved for NYHA class I-III patients.

source_text: Benefit has not been observed in patients with class IV symptoms, severe aortic stenosis, or impaired renal function (eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2 body surface area).

logic_node.action: Avoid tafamidis with severely impaired renal function
logic_node.action_detail: Benefit of tafamidis has not been observed in patients with impaired renal function (eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2). Such patients should not be expected to benefit from tafamidis therapy.

source_text: Benefit has not been observed in patients with class IV symptoms, severe aortic stenosis, or impaired renal function (eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2 body surface area).

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiac amyloidosis and atrial fibrillation, anticoagulation is reasonable to reduce the risk of stroke regardless of the CHA2DS2-VASc score. Intracardiac thrombosis occurs in approximately one-third of patients with cardiac amyloidosis, in some cases in the absence of diagnosed AF. DOAC vs warfarin choice has not been studied in ATTR-CM.

source_text: In patients with cardiac amyloidosis and AF, anticoagulation is reasonable to reduce the risk of stroke regardless of the CHA2DS2-VASc score.

logic_node.action: Use caution with standard HFrEF GDMT in ATTR-CM
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with ATTR-CM and LVEF <=40%, GDMT may be poorly tolerated. The vasodilating effects of ARNi, ACEi, and ARB may exacerbate hypotension, especially with amyloid-associated autonomic dysfunction. Beta blockers may worsen HF symptoms as patients with ATTR-CM rely on heart rate response to maintain cardiac output. ICD benefit is unclear. CRT has not been studied in ATTR-CM with HFrEF.

source_text: For patients with ATTR-CM and EF <= 40%, GDMT may be poorly tolerated. The vasodilating effects of ARNi, ACEi, and ARB may exacerbate hypotension. Beta blockers may worsen HF symptoms as patients rely on heart rate response.

logic_node.action: Consider inotersen or patisiran for ATTRv with polyneuropathy
logic_node.action_detail: Inotersen and patisiran (TTR silencers that disrupt hepatic synthesis via mRNA inhibition/degradation) are approved for ATTRv with polyneuropathy. They are associated with slower progression of amyloidosis-related polyneuropathy. Ongoing trials are evaluating their impact on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

source_text: Therapies inotersen and patisiran are presently approved only for ATTRv with polyneuropathy. Inotersen and patisiran are associated with slower progression of amyloidosis-related polyneuropathy in ATTRv-CM.

logic_node.action_detail: AL amyloidosis is treatable, and patients with AL amyloidosis with cardiac involvement should promptly be referred to hematology-oncology for timely treatment. AL-CM is managed by hematology-oncology specialists and is beyond the scope of cardiologists, though diagnosis is often made by cardiologists.

source_text: AL amyloidosis is treatable, and patients with AL amyloidosis with cardiac involvement should promptly be referred to hematology-oncology for timely treatment.

logic_node.action: Identify clinical features suggesting cardiac amyloidosis
logic_node.action_detail: Clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis should be raised with LV wall thickness >=14 mm in conjunction with fatigue, dyspnea, or edema, especially with discordance between wall thickness on echocardiogram and QRS voltage on ECG, apical sparing of LV longitudinal strain on echocardiography, diffuse late-gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI, and in the context of aortic stenosis, HFpEF, carpal tunnel syndrome, spinal stenosis, or autonomic/sensory polyneuropathy.

source_text: LV wall thickness >=14 mm in conjunction with fatigue, dyspnea, or edema, especially in the context of discordance between wall thickness on echocardiogram and QRS voltage on ECG, and in the context of aortic stenosis, HFpEF, carpal tunnel syndrome.
